releases.name: OpenWork v0.18.60
releases.body:
## Move older OpenWork installs to OpenCode v2 in the background

- **Older installs move to OpenCode v2 in the background.** Existing installs still using OpenCode v1 are moved over automatically, with a backup made first so your chats are kept. Windows installers also carry less duplicate engine data, and Windows can identify OpenWork's signed app files.
- **Computer use is more capable and predictable.** For Mac users, the agent can script apps directly and keeps working while you use your computer; Take over and Stop return control, and Continue resumes the task. Workbot can also script supported desktop apps. Browser pages keep a steady desktop, tablet, or phone size while the panel changes, and forms take fewer steps. When available, you can dictate into OpenWork or Workbot.
- **Chat can work with more of your existing tasks and connections.** Type `#` to add another task as context, ask the agent to create or move sidebar groups, and find connected actions with everyday wording. You can finish or repair an API-key connection in chat without sharing the key with the agent, and OpenWork Cloud tools work again in older desktop versions.
- **Documents and first launches are more dependable.** Closing an edited document now gives clear save, discard, or cancel choices, and reloading or reopening it preserves your editing session and unsaved work. Workbot can open a requested document beside chat, explain why a file could not open, and show or rebuild a computer that will not connect. Fresh desktop installs can load built-in tools even if the package registry is unavailable; slow Windows sign-in and first launch no longer hide recovery options.
- **For admins: team and organization controls are clearer.** Platform administrators can manage feature access per organization member and, when enabled, grant organizations Web access or extra Free Auto usage. Admins can finish connector setup after a check fails, remove connectors, and save team-role changes reliably; Workbot settings show one default model and its availability. When available, Workbot can guide eligible people from free Auto to paid Luna without losing the conversation.
- **Website visitors can find practical AI governance guidance.** The expanded enterprise pages explain governing employee AI and planning an OpenWork rollout.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.59...v0.18.60)

*Windows installers are signed using Microsoft Artifact Signing.*


## Known open fixes
Shipped without (decided by Ben, 2026-10-22: none is a regression introduced since v0.18.59; all are older fork PRs still in review): #6043, #5915, #5749, #5613, #4680, #4215, #4061, #4009, #4007, #4005, #3970, #3903, #3781, #3595, #3414, #3413. No PR opened since v0.18.59 matched the release fix filter.

releases.name: OpenWork v0.18.59
releases.body:
## Read, edit, and discuss documents in Workbot

- **Work on documents without leaving Workbot.** When Documents is enabled for your workspace, preview Drive files before choosing Edit when editing is enabled, keep chat open beside a document, and continue your conversation with the file in view. Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides stay in Google and save to the original; on OpenWork Cloud, Office files can use an editor in your own workspace when enabled.
- **AI models and providers work more smoothly across OpenWork.** Desktop users can use existing Azure Foundry and custom OpenAI-compatible providers on OpenCode v2, see organization model changes in the picker when enabled, and find the same available models in Settings and shortcuts. When AI Gateway access is enabled, cloud agents can use supported models assigned by their organization.
- **Admins can check setup before work gets stuck.** Settings › Diagnostics brings desktop startup, AI provider, connector, and deployment-service checks together. Google Workspace settings can also identify APIs an admin needs to turn on, and Workbot explains when an organization needs an AI provider before it can answer.
- **Chat keeps files, prompts, and agent work on track.** Files saved from chat go to the opened folder, including files created in a conversation's own folder; links with spaces open correctly, failed writes are labeled as failed, and messages in side chats are easier to start. OpenCode v2 history copies can resume after restart; if a chat is too large to copy whole, its largest outputs or attachments stay in the original history.
- **Team and Workbot tasks have clearer paths.** When enabled, members can connect assigned accounts in Workbot; members with team-management access can open the right team's settings, and teams can follow tasks started on another computer. When available, admins can set team or organization defaults for new desktop chats and provider-specific spend limits, and inspect Library use and free Auto conversion insights. Workbot's link-only sharing is gone; authorized invitation emails remain available in Den.
- **Self-hosting and connected tools get practical fixes.** Self-hosters get updated AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure deployment options and clearer service checks. MCP clients can identify OpenWork and receive clearer tool guidance, and the website's Trust Center links now lead to the hosted Trust Center.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.58...v0.18.59)

releases.name: OpenWork v0.18.58
releases.body:
## Run OpenWork Web on your own self-hosted deployment

- **Self-host OpenWork Web and team tools on AWS.** For self-hosters: run OpenWork Web with sandboxed browser workspaces, and deploy Slack, Workbot, and Automations that run without a desktop. AWS deployments can use existing networks and load balancers, and can connect to an existing cluster or runner fleet.
- **Connect OpenCode 2 to your organization.** If you use OpenWork from OpenCode: the `opencode-openwork` plugin brings in your organization's AI Gateway models, tools, and skills after sign-in, without the desktop app. You can also upgrade desktop chats to OpenCode 2 with a backup first; its conversations can use the built-in browser and discover connected tools reliably.
- **Admins get clearer controls and reporting.** Organization Analytics is back, with restored usage and workflow history where available. When enabled, admins can also report on skills, plugins, and connectors, set member, admin, and team permissions, and choose a default model for cloud agents; Audit Logs now cover more organization activity.
- **Chat and daily work recover more smoothly.** Pasted text and images stay at the cursor, reopened Apps load their data, migrated chats with a missing agent can answer again, and OpenWork keeps the Working status visible during quiet stretches. Ollama keeps multiple selected models and their thinking choices; Drive uploads respect your chosen Google account.
- **Calendar, Workbot, and connections do more.** When Calendar features are enabled, add or edit Automations alongside meetings; Workbot can recover stopped tasks. When enabled, admins can check when connections were last verified, and compatible MCP clients can subscribe to remote-session updates.
- **Some familiar pages and searches have changed.** Organization dashboards and admin-assigned dashboards in Desktop are gone, while personal dashboards remain. “Search sessions” now searches session titles and workspace names, not message text; for organizations with OpenWork Models, Auto is replaced in the model picker by GPT-6 Luna.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.57...v0.18.58)

releases.name: OpenWork v0.18.57
releases.body:
## Move your Claude Cowork setup to OpenWork with one prompt

- **Move your Cowork setup with one prompt.** Ask the agent you already use to follow `openworklabs.com/migrate.md` to bring your Claude Cowork and Claude Code plugins and skills into OpenWork. Re-running picks up changes without duplicates, reuses connections your organization already has, and explains when a connection still needs setup.
- **Give each teammate their own connector key.** For admins: external connections can use individual keys instead of one shared key. Members can add or replace their key from the Library or Den, using a masked entry form; desktop chat can guide them to add one when needed. For admins who use LiteLLM, connecting your own proxy is also available as a preview on request.
- **Auto and Apps are available to more organizations.** Free Auto no longer needs an organization-by-organization rollout, and every organization can build Apps without a platform admin enabling them. Auto can also read images you attach or that tools return, and signed-out Linux desktops no longer need a system keyring to use it.
- **Self-hosting gains a Google Cloud Run starting point.** For self-hosters: starter deployment files and instructions cover the Den API, Den web app, and migration job on Cloud Run. Old self-hosted Den settings that had no effect are no longer read.
- **Everyday work is clearer and more dependable.** Your first organization message now gets an answer before you have a workspace; videos made in a conversation's work folder play in chat; and stopping a run no longer leaves a bold “Step interrupted” row. Agent-led installs open on Setup complete without requiring Node first, and teammate invites survive workspace claiming. Model names and provider details are clearer. Workbot uses one quiet activity line and can react with emoji, while Slack runs wait for slow desktop work instead of reporting that they are stuck.
- **Some desktop options have changed or are gone.** Workspace sharing and remote-workspace connections have been removed. Organization Analytics is gone, while usage reporting remains in AI Gateway. Plugins now come from your organization's Library instead of being installed into workspaces, and the “From GitHub” plugin import is gone. The Library no longer has a card view. Automation choices now say Desktop or Cloud, and computer use has been removed from that editor.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.56...v0.18.57)
